# Question: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Rival: copy the upper output half vertically

A strong simple candidate is **copy_upper_half**: apply the reflected-fill rule
using row frontiers from the upper half of the occupied vertical span, then copy
those rows to the lower half. In equivalent terms, replace each lower row frontier
with its upper mirrored partner's frontier. **copy_lower_half** is the analogous
competitor in the other direction. The claim is a plausible and reproduced shortcut,
not a ranking over every imaginable program.

All four usable canonical pairs (three demos plus the canonical test pair) have
vertically symmetric frontiers, so both competitors match4/4. A no-op or a rule
that fills only to the reflection axis does not have that property. Canonical-fit
results are retained in checks/final-probe.json and the full production census.

## Exact counterexample from the ORIGINAL generator

Task66e63986855b, original generator SHA `6493cddafa2f41ce449da8edec78bb1c40528c7c5a1be459371c4d089164cee3`,
rulee9ecd02cbe2e, seed0, difficulty easy, sample_index3, no overrides. Rows below
are single-digit ARC cells; the grid has7rows×9columns.

Input:
```text
888800000
888000000
880000000
888000000
880000000
888800000
000000000
```

Actual canonical Racket output:
```text
000000000
000880000
008888000
000880000
008888000
000000000
000000000
```

Wrong upper-half-copy output:
```text
000000000
000880000
008888000
008888000
000880000
000000000
000000000
```

The occupied row frontiers are[3,2,1,2,1,3]. The true rule processes each interior
row independently: with R=3, fill r+1..6-r inclusive. Upper-copy wrongly swaps the
widths on lower interior rows3 and4 (zero-based), giving four wrong cells overall.
The original three preceding draws at indices0,1,2 match the rival perfectly;
this is a genuine ambiguous three-demo/one-query lesson, not just a stand-alone
input where an arbitrary rule differs. See checks/baseline-lessons.json for every
input, actual label, rival output, index, and grid hash. Equivalent seed0 witnesses
also occur at medium start17 and hard start22.

## How the output was checked

The12inputs from all three exact lessons were submitted to the public Racket command
from the packet root:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 66e63986855b --input ../checks/baseline-lesson-inputs.json --out ../checks/baseline-lesson-racket.json
```

The payload ran from repo. The receipt records baseline generator identity,
executed canonical rule hash, exact input/output grids and hashes, and successful
outputs; all12agree with the saved mirror. It is not merely a comparison between
two Python implementations. No solve-private labels were accessed for this probe.

## Does the repair emit distinguishing cases?

Yes. Final v4 SHA `8f78ef0944e40e80f9b86e9d5fdb2c9515fd05240e400d097e9993c5af79bc2f` forces asymmetric_front
on default odd raw indices, across all three bands. All three original seed/start
recipes are replayed by regressions and are now distinguished under every holdout
(the v4 inputs differ because versioned keyed RNG is expected to change).
The claim is emission of this distinguishing asymmetric family, not replay of an
old pixel array under a new version salt.

The raw probe enumerated1,152overlapping windows and4,608rotations from1,728draws
(1,554unique inputs; seeds700000..700063, six starts, all bands), with zero measured
ambiguity for actual declared rivals. The separate production/Racket census gave
300lessons,1,200rotations,1,166unique inputs and no ambiguous rotations. All accepted
indices are recorded and no pairs were rejected in that population. Both mirrored
half-copy rules are refuted by the retained demonstration witnesses.

The finite-rival and assembly limitations remain explicit. Exact profile overrides
can intentionally request only symmetric inputs, and arbitrary dropped/reordered
pairs are not covered by the raw consecutive-draw guarantee.
